question.worked_solution:
First, we bring the quotient under a single radical and then simplify the result:

$$
\frac{\sqrt{32{z}^{5}}}{\sqrt{8{z}^{3}}}=\sqrt{\frac{32{z}^{5}}{8{z}^{3}}}=\sqrt{4{z}^{2}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{4{z}^{2}} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}{z}^{2}} & = \\ \sqrt{{(2z)}^{2}} & = \\ |2z| & = \\ |2|\cdot |z| & = \\ 2\cdot |z| & \end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we are told that $z>0,$ so we have $|z|=z.$ Therefore, the final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |z| & = \\ 2\cdot z & = \\ 2z.\end{aligned}
$$
